references.text: The context that identifies the men who brought a bad report about the land, the ten spies who discouraged the people from entering Canaan.
Describes how the spies spread a bad report (דִּבָּה) about the land among the children of Israel.
Another plague (מַגֵּפָה) that struck the people as a result of rebellion against the Lord.
Yet another plague (מַגֵּפָה) that the Lord sent as punishment for Israel's sin.
The Lord threatens to strike the people with pestilence, showing God's judgment on disobedience.
A reference to the plague at Peor, an example of God's punishment over sin in Israel.
A poetic retelling of how plagues came upon Israel because of their actions.
Paul warns against grumbling as the Israelites did, and refers to the destroyer who struck them down.
Refers to those who sinned in the wilderness and were not allowed to enter rest because of unbelief.
